limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account as the producer. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. Same-host agent reviewer. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file, and never read the Kimi home or the retained scratch directories. Code and documents were read from a snapshot (commit 29b7cfc; not checked against git). Private scratch files were deleted.

This is a delta review of kimi-public-candidates-v4 against the approved v3 and its review kimi-independent-public-review-v3. Delta review: the semantic checks of earlier reviews carry over only for files that are byte-equal. 183 of 200 files are byte-equal to v3: all native files, all inputs (observer, workload, context, capture documents, assertion, transformation receipt), the logs and the file histories. The 17 files that differ are, per run: manifest.json, the bound adapter document (runtime/docs/survival-v1/adapters/kimi.md) and the bound source runtime/session_bench/kimi_score_inputs.py (both equal to the snapshot at 29b7cfc); plus the bundle (public-inputs-candidate.json: the digest of the adapter document in the format locator, 3 values), summary.json and, per run, the replay receipt and the private-transformation sidecar (a parent manifest digest). The reviewer re-read them. Sets v1, v2 and v3 must never be published; previous sets that held a private-derived value must never be published (set v2 held the localDate value).

Change 1, localDate. In the injected date message of the wire log, the value of localDate is blanked at equal length (10 characters, as the time zone name beside it), in all three runs; it was the only changed line of the log (123 lines, byte length equal). The reviewer searched the private localDate value and the private time zone name in all 200 files (also in hex, base64 and UTF-16 form): the time zone name occurs nowhere; the date string occurs only in the bound adapter document, as part of the ids of two unused controller attempts (kimi-2026-10-07-01 and -02) and in the text of the schema-stability window, never as a statement of the local date of a scored run. The key name localDate stays in the log, as the key timeZone does, because it is the vendor structure; it also occurs as text in the bound adapter document, which states the blanking. Every time stamp with a zone suffix in the set ends in Z (UTC); no other local time or UTC offset is present. The run ids appear to use the UTC date (inferred; the scored run kimi-2026-10-08-01 began at 2026-10-08T02:21Z); the attempt ids therefore do not give the local date either. Kept: the length of the time zone name (19 characters) and of the date (10).

Change of this set, edit-argument guard. check_observed_edit_arguments (kimi_score_inputs.py) now raises when an observed edit action has no input, an empty input or an input that is not a JSON object; before, it skipped such an edit. build_kimi_replay_evidence now raises when the check compared no edit although the workload instance has an action of kind edit. Controls the reviewer ran, by calling the functions of each packet's own runtime copy (the module path was asserted to lie inside the packet) on modified copies of the observer document and the decoded native record, in all three runs: baseline compares 1 edit; missing input, empty input, string input, list input and null input each raise 'Kimi observed edit has no arguments'; one changed character of the observer new text, an extra key in the observer input, one changed character of the native old text, and a removed native record each raise; an observer with the edit event removed, an edit event retyped to another action kind, and a missing input each make build_kimi_replay_evidence raise (the first two with 'compared no edit although the workload has a scored edit'). The count-only check without the workload still returns 0 when no edit event exists, so the 'no edit compared' rule lives in build_kimi_replay_evidence only. Canary: a scratch rebuild of a packet whose runtime copy raises a canary error at the start of check_observed_edit_arguments fails the whole replay with the canary message, so the check runs inside the replay; the same scratch rebuild with the unmodified runtime reproduces the public manifest byte for byte. A byte change of a pinned file is rejected by the pins before the check is reached (as in the earlier review), so the function-level tests above are the proof of the guard. Wording note: the adapter document says the old check skipped such an edit 'until set v3'; set v3 is the last set with the skip, v4 is the first without it. No metric row changes: all 31 rows of the three runs equal the saved replays of v3 (91.222, 91.239, 91.245; aggregate 91.235); only the digests of the adapter document in the format evidence locators, the manifests and the receipts differ.

Schema stability (3 points). The evidence inside a packet still holds one observation, its own run. The window check over the unused sessions is not recomputed by the closed replay, because those sessions are in no packet: it rests on the producer's test, on the adapter document and on this reviewer's own run. The two sessions of 2026-09-29 with a wire log are outside the declared window; they hold no record type outside the contract either.

Environment of the runs: Kimi Code CLI 2.1.1 in an isolated home, Moonshot API, model kimi-k2.7-code, one build, one day, one machine, one account with a limit of 3 requests a minute. Capture authenticity rests on the producer's capture documents. The plan binds the controller source by SHA-256; runs 1 and 2 used that file about 15 minutes before it was committed (same bytes).

Run selection. Three of six attempts of 2026-10-08 are scored (the first, second and sixth); two more attempts of 2026-10-07 failed by a controller setting. The rubric rule against replacing a scheduled run is waived for v1 by owner decision, made after the results were known; the reviewer cannot verify that decision. Each stated reason was checked in the capture files: four attempts stopped at the provider rate limit and one ended turn 1 without the required marker. None holds a complete two-turn session. In each the native record agrees with the stdout stream for everything that happened.

Rules chosen after the captures. The read (wire.jsonl and state.json), the exit-code rule and the root were chosen after the files of the captures had been seen. Duplicate safety is 0 of 14 under any read of this format.

Root, accepted with reservation (3 points, and the row becomes provisional if refused). The declared root is the session directory; it is complete and equal to its source by SHA-256. Two kinds of file of the isolated home name the session and were listed but not copied: sessions/.index-cache/scan.json and the query cache. In a whole-home copy of the same build they hold only id, workspace, cwd, times and lastTurnReason, and the listed sizes of the three runs fit that layout, so there is no room for a usage field. The bytes are not bound. If a reader counts them as part of the root, portable.complete_root is lost and attribution.reconciliation (native_absent) becomes unresolved. The Claude Code CLI row also declares a session-level root inside a larger home.

Exit code 0, accepted (about 8.3 points if refused). A successful shell result holds no isError and no exit code; the decoder reads status success and exit code 0. A failed result holds isError true and the code in its text. The Claude Code and Cursor CLI rows read the same case the same way, and the helper ledger agrees in every run.

Usage judgments accepted. inputOther is taken as the input count (9 points if refused). inputCacheCreation is 0 in every usage record of every capture; the key is written, a cache write was never reported, and the rubric gives credit for the key (4 points if a reader requires proof that the 0 is measured). Reconciliation is native_absent and is not too low: no record declares a usage total; token_counting.turn_recorded is the context size, and the usage records of a turn do not sum to it.

Other scoring judgments accepted. The response marker is taken from the native text; the full native text equals the observed text in all six responses (about 13 points in repetition 3 without the rule). protocol_version is the format version, one value seen (4 points). The harness name comes from the first sentence of the system prompt (2 points). The format document is the adapter document in the packet (2 points). The changed file comes from the explicit contentHash values (4 points). The model joins by turnStep (3 points). The seven retried requests of repetition 1 hold no event content and are metadata.

Observer. It is rebuilt in the closed replay from the launch receipts, the stdout stream of each turn, the helper ledger and the workspace file hashes; no native file is read. The stream is written by the same process as the native record. It has no status field: exit codes and output lines come from the helper ledger, and the edit status rests on the changed file hash. The observed edit action holds its arguments, and the replay compares them with the native arguments; the guard now also fails on a missing or empty input and on a replay that compared no edit. The edit path in the observer arguments is a scratch directory name that also appears in the packet (kept on purpose).

Public derivative, not raw capture. At equal byte length: the home name is aliased; the system prompt after its first sentence, 660 tool and schema descriptions and 9 injected messages are blanked; digests of blanked text and of files outside the packets are zeroed; the time zone name and the localDate of the injected date message are blanked; the organisation id and the key id of provider error messages are aliased. Kept on purpose: the first sentence of the system prompt (15 words, vendor text beside the fragments that the handover names; the owner must confirm it and the report must name it), provider message ids (a time, a server value and a counter), the scratch directory names (they appear in the edit path of the observer too), session ids and capture times in UTC.

Privacy checks and their limits. No home name, home path, e-mail, organisation id, key id, time zone name, local date or token pattern was found in the 200 files of the set directory (the 186 packet files, the bundle and the sidecars) in plain, lower, upper, reversed, hex, base64 (three alignments, URL-safe), UTF-16 (both byte orders), percent and SHA-1/256/512/MD5 forms. Values of id-like keys of the private parent (7) occur only as the 6 provider message ids (kept on purpose, class message id) and the name of the environment variable that holds the API key (a name, not a value); the organisation id and the key id of the private parent (3 forms found by pattern) and the operator e-mail occur in none of the files. Every /Users/ path holds the alias. check_public_packets passes as the sanitizer calls it (the sanitizer's DIGEST_ALLOWLIST and HEX_ALLOWLIST, the three fresh replay receipts, the bundle as extra file): 902 public-bytes digests, 11 replay-output digests, 3 allowlisted vendor package digests (not checked against the registry), no unbound digest, no unlisted hex run (decimal 489, constant 9, derivable 66, uuid 398, allowlisted 40); short_digest_warnings is empty; the classes equal summary.json and v3. The API key was never available to the reviewer, so only token patterns were searched. A scan cannot prove the absence of a private value in a form that was not tried.

Locator binding. The observer sha256 in the bundle equals inputs/observer.json of each packet. 531 locators of the three pairs were resolved: whole-file locators, the 303 wire-log line locators (sha of the line), the documentation locator (the bound adapter document), the rule locators, and the 12 'outside-the-read' locators, whose digest is the SHA-256 of the JSON pair [name, size] of a file that is not opened (as in the decoder, and as in v3). All equal. The fixed label kimi-isolated-home-receipts on 12 observer id lists is a bundle label, not an id in observer.json (as v3).

Never publish the sidecar files beside the packets (summary.json, *-private-transformation.json, *-receipt.json, *-tamper.json), the private parents kimi-score-replay-v1 to -v4, or the sets v1, v2 and v3 (superseded; set v2 holds the localDate value).
